newsitem.title: GERMANY: EU fishmeal tight as Peru's fishing ban continues.
newsitem.headline: EU fishmeal tight as Peru's fishing ban continues.

text.p: Fishmeal prices in northern European feeds markets were buoyed by signs a Peruvian fishing ban would last longer than expected, traders said.
The ban had been in place since early August and was due to be lifted in early or mid-October, they said.
"It might take until the middle of November as it seems they are only now sending out boats to test the location and size of the stocks," one said.
Peruvian fishmeal over the last month has risen $20 cif northern Europe to $620.
Chile has been supplying meal to the world market in recent weeks but preferred Asian buyers who were paying premiums for special qualities, traders said.
Bremen/Hamburg meal markets have not quoted Chilean meal since mid-October.
Any origin fishmeal (64 percent) in bulk free on truck or fob was last quoted at 95-97 marks/100 kg for 1996 dates, having risen by up to 2.50 marks over the last 10 days.
Traders were divided over the impact of the tightness.
One believed soymeal, rapemeal and feedgrain could easily replace the animal protein in compound feed mixtures.
But another said, "My customers insist on two to three percent fishmeal in their mixes."
